_comment: EACH DEVICE ITS JOB (DR-0678). Darrell 2026-09-29: "Laptop for creating... we need to be able to use the devices appropriately". pipeline-nodes.json says WHICH machines exist; this file says what each CLASS of device is FOR, and which app surfaces it is best for, and why. The app reads it (app/src/lib/device-roles.js) to decide what comes FIRST and how it is laid out. It never decides what is ALLOWED: every surface stays reachable on every device (the never-blocked rule, pinned by app/src/__tests__/device-roles.test.js). No addresses, no users, no secrets here: this file ships in the public bundle.

phone.label: Phone
phone.why: It is in his hand when the word comes. A phone has a microphone and a thumb, not a keyboard: it catches a lesson the moment it is spoken, plays one back on the road, and answers a waiting decision with one tap. Long comparison and merging are cramped at 390px and wait for the laptop, one link away.

surfaces.why: Thinking Space holds the one input box: speak or type, and the Lesson chip sends it to the lesson intake.
The Create station opens with the recorder and the lessons waiting on a decision, and hands a long review to the laptop.
Listen to anything in the chosen voice, hands free.

tablet.label: Tablet
tablet.why: A middle screen with touch and no keyboard: wide enough to read a lesson whole and to look over a version, not built for long typing. Recorded here so a folded-open phone or a tablet gets a sensible order instead of a guess.

surfaces.why: The lessons read whole at a comfortable width.
Record, and look over a lesson's versions.

laptop.label: Laptop or desktop
laptop.why: Laptop for creating. A wide screen shows two writers' versions side by side, a real keyboard writes and edits long-form, and a fine pointer selects exactly. This is where a lesson is written, compared across the LLMs that drafted it, merged, and published, and where the Governor works his decision queue.

surfaces.why: The Create station: lesson entry, Your lessons (compare, merge, publish), the decision queues and the towers, laid out across the width with keyboard shortcuts.
The Governor's full decision queue and the lessons waiting on his word.
The operations board: what the NAS and the towers are doing.

tv.label: TV or Firestick
tv.why: Read across the room and heard in the voice. A remote has arrows and OK, no keyboard and no pointer, so the TV reads and plays; signing in and anything that needs typing are done from the phone in his hand (DR-0658).

surfaces.why: The Living Lessons, read large and read aloud.

nas.label: NAS
nas.why: Always on. The lessons, the recordings and the services that turn a spoken word into a lesson live here (DR-0677); the app reaches it through the same-origin transport, never directly.

surfaces.why: Its health and what it is doing, read live on the operations board.

tower.label: Tower
tower.why: The RTX 4070 towers run the models: the Ollama lesson writers and OpenClaw on tlcmediadpt. The right tower feeds the wall and live work always wins it (DR-0012).

surfaces.why: The towers' state and parity, on the operations board.
The Towers panel shows which writers ran, beside the versions they wrote.

record.label: Record or type a lesson
record.why: Where a lesson begins: spoken or typed, sent to the lesson intake.

your-lessons.label: Your lessons
your-lessons.why: Each lesson from arrival to live, and every writer's version side by side to compare, merge and publish (DR-0672).

decide.label: Lessons to decide
decide.why: Lessons with more than one version, waiting for the Governor's decision.

governor.label: Governor's decision queue
governor.why: The decisions only the Governor makes, batched.

towers.label: Towers
towers.why: Which tower wrote what, and whether the towers agree.

read-listen.label: Read and listen
read-listen.why: The lessons to read and hear.

handoff.label: Continue on another device
handoff.why: Send the work to the device that suits it.

laptop_note: No laptop is recorded in pipeline-nodes.json as of 2026-09-29. The two 'workstation' nodes (tlc-tech-team, kingdom-home) have unconfirmed roles and are not assumed to be his laptop. The app does not need a named laptop to know it is on one: it measures the screen. Naming the laptop matters only for the fleet witness.
